Excerpts:
--- doc_id: STATUTE-bsa-s92 | The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 — Section 92 (Presumption as to documents thirty years old) (Unknown Court, 2023-12-25) | section: Presumption as to documents thirty years old ---
Where any document, purporting or proved to be thirty years old, is produced from any custody which the Court in the particular case considers proper, the Court may presume that the signature and every other part of such document, which purports to be in the handwriting of any particular person, is in that person’s handwriting, and, in the case of a document executed or attested, that it was duly executed and attested by the persons by whom it purports to be executed and attested. Explanation.--The Explanation to section 80 shall also apply to this section. Illustrations. (a) A has been in possession of landed property for a long time. He produces from his custody deeds relating to the land showing his titles to it. The custody shall be proper. (b) A produces deeds relating to landed property of which he is the mortgagee. The mortgagor is in possession. The custody shall be proper. (c) A, a connection of B, produces deeds relating to lands in B's possession, which were deposited with him by B for safe custody. The custody shall be proper.

--- doc_id: STATUTE-bsa-s78 | The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 — Section 78 (Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies) (Unknown Court, 2023-12-25) | section: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies ---
(1) The Court shall presume to be genuine every document purporting to be a certificate, certified copy or other document, which is by law declared to be admissible as evidence of any particular fact and which purports to be duly certified by any officer of the Central Government or of a State Government: Provided that such document is substantially in the form and purports to be executed in the manner directed by law in that behalf. (2) The Court shall also presume that any officer by whom any such document purports to be signed or certified, held, when he signed it, the official character wh

--- doc_id: STATUTE-bsa-s80 | The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 — Section 80 (Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents) (Unknown Court, 2023-12-25) | section: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents ---
The Court shall presume the genuineness of every document purporting to be the Official Gazette, or to be a newspaper or journal, and of every document purporting to be a document directed by any law to be kept by any person, if such document is kept substantially in the form required by law and is produced from proper custody. Explanation.--For the purposes of this section and section 92, document is said to be in proper custody if it is in the place in which, and looked after by the person with whom such document is required to be kept; but no custody is improper if it is proved to have had a legitimate origin, or if the circumstances of the particular case are such as to render that origin probable.

Question: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, when can a court presume that a document is genuine merely because it is thirty years old and was produced from proper custody, without any witness proving its execution?

- Be concise: aim for 500 to 1,200 characters. Go longer only when the legal issue genuinely needs it. Never repeat a point, a caveat or a conclusion.
- Use only the excerpts above. Do not mention any Act, section, case or citation that does not appear in them.
- Mark every supported claim with [n]. When the answer compares or relies on several provisions or judgments, cite each one where it is used. Keep what the excerpts establish separate from anything they do not address.
- Stop once the question is answered: no closing recap, "Thus"/"Therefore" summary or "Conclusion" section that repeats earlier sentences.
- If the excerpts do not answer the question, reply in at most three sentences (about 500 characters): what they do establish [n] and, once, what is missing. Do not restate the gap, add a conclusion, or speculate.
- Use "### " headings only when the answer has several distinct parts.

### Meaning of "proper custody"
The Explanation to Section 80, made applicable to Section 92, clarifies that custody is proper if the document is kept in the place, and looked after by the person, with whom it is required to be kept; custody is not rendered improper merely because of some irregularity, so long as the document is shown to have had a legitimate origin, or the circumstances of the case render such an origin probable[2].

### Illustrations
Section 92 itself illustrates proper custody: a person in long-standing possession of land producing title deeds from his own custody; a mortgagee producing deeds relating to property in the mortgagor's possession; and a person producing deeds deposited with him by a connection for safe custody—in each case the custody is treated as proper[1]."}
